झष: Jhaṣa is mentioned in the story of Manu told in the Śata-patha Brāhmaṇa,^1 where it means a ‘great fish’ (mahā-matsya) according to the commentator. Eggeling^2 suggests that a horned fish is meant, because in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā^3 the Iḍā, or personified libation, is represented as a cow, and this may have brought in the idea of a horned fish in the later form of an old legend. But cf. Jaṣa. 1) i. 8, 1, 4. 2) Sacred Books of the East, 12, 217, n. 3; 26, xxxi. 3) i. 7, 1; ii. 6, 7.
